study type: clinical trial (not specified, but likely randomized)
cohort: 150 nulliparous women between 37 and 42 weeks of gestation with singleton, viable, vertex presentation, and no history of uterine surgery, uterine anomalies, or congenital anomalies.
finding: There was no significant difference between high- and low-dose oxytocin induction protocols in terms of cesarean section rates, maternal and fetal complications.
mod_finding: High-dose oxytocin induction significantly shortened the second stage of labor but did not show a difference in the duration of the first stage of active labor compared to low-dose oxytocin.
